body:
I think, this modification breaks the default behaviour:
https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2e3ac70e0af46640c2606c5e49bf695745db2278#diff-e1329c3d217826f2cddc8d77b4374ad8L132

I think you have a misunderstanding about how ngClass works. Here's an explanation (quite old though) https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/5763#issuecomment-166114033. Basically you're saying: "I want this class to be added when it's false", and in your case it's always false, therefore it will always be there.

See this [example](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-9a4jrd?file=icon/icon.component.ts) where I simply pass a toggling variable for the "large" property (the same thing you're doing with the "show" property).
Could be a valid bug, simpler repro: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-xybndc?file=app/app.component.html

thanks, @pkozlowski-opensource. But we are not first and not last who will face with this problem. It's look like a bug, if not, browser console should show descriptive error maybe? Because it's not obvious

> But we are not first and not last who will face with this problem. It's look like a bug, if not browser console should show descriptive error maybe? Because it's not obvious

Totally. We should look into this one to see if we can handle this case correctly and add an error message if not.
